info.description: # Overview We've included as much technical information about the FMDB Pro API as we can. If you have any questions though, please contact us. ## API Authentication All API Requests are authenticated by an API Key. To do this, each HTTP request must include a parameter named `x-api-key` in the `HEADER` of any request which includes the API Key string. To receive an API Key, please contact the FMDB Pro team. ## API Versions For all data requests, you can set a version by adding a parameter named `x-api-version` in the `HEADER` of any request. Omitting this from the header will return the latest version. # Data Requests The FMDB Pro API provides a robust and flexible query mechanism that allows you to filter, sort, and paginate the data returned. ## Pagination Requests can be paginated by either pages or using continuation tokens using a combination of the following; | Parameter | Default | Description | Example | |----------|----------|----------|----------| |`pageSize` | `20` | Specifies the number of records to return per request. Max 500. | `GET /api/?pageSize=10` | |`page` | `1` | Specifies which number page of data to return. This parameter cannot be used in conjunction with `continuation` and `continuationToken` parameters. | `GET /api/?page=2` | | or | |`continuation` | `false` | This parameter activates the "pagination by cursor" functionality, that has better performance when retrieving larger datasets. When set to `true` the meta object in the response will contain a `continuationToken` that can be used to retrieve the next page at a significantly faster speed. If the `continuationToken` field is `null` it means that there's no more pages to fetch. | `GET /api/?continuation=true` | |`continuationToken` | `null` | Specifies the token to retrieve the next page of a continuous call. This parameter must be used with `continuation=true` and cannot be used in conjunction with `page`. | `GET /api/?continuation=true&continuationToken=XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX` | It is recommended that you use `continuation` and `continuationToken` for larger API requests. Technical Note: The continuation tokens do not work with the `pageSize` parameter. It will return an optimal amount of data per request depending on the dataset queried. e.g. The larger `players` endpoint dataset will return fewer results than the `clubs` endpoint due to the amount of data in each response but will be at a reliable and stable response time. ## Sorting Requests can be sorted on single or multiple fields by using comma seperated field names. e.g. `?sortOrder=name,age&sortBy=ASC,DESC` would sort by `name` ascending and then `age` descending. | Parameter | Description | Example | |----------|----------|----------| |`sortBy` | Which field to sort the data on. Can have multiple comma seperated values. | `GET /api/?sortBy=name` | |`sortOrder` | Sort order direction. Can have multiple comma seperated values. Defaults to `ASC` | `GET /api/?sortBy=name&sortOrder=DESC` | Note: Sorting cannot be used with `continuation` and `continuationToken`. ## Shaping You can shape the response by optionally including or excluding fields and objects. | Parameter | Description | Example | |----------|----------|----------| |`includeFields` | Include only these fields in the response. The usage is limited to the first-level fields of the object requested; it is not possible to reshape nested objects. The parameter accepts a comma separated list of fields. | `GET /api/?includeFields=id,name,age` | |`excludeFields` | Exclude these fields from the response. The usage is limited to the first-level fields of the object requested; it is not possible to reshape nested objects. The parameter accepts a comma separated list of fields. | `GET /api/?excludeFields=nationality,secondNationality` | ## Filters All fields can be searched by their name for an exact match; | Parameter | Description | Example | |----------|----------|----------| |`` | Filters the data based on whether the field's value matches the specified value. | `GET /api/?name=John` | You can also search for `null` values using: | Parameter | Description | Example | |----------|----------|----------| |`Null` | Filters the data based on whether the field's value is NULL. | `GET /api/?nameNull=true` | Every filter condition can be negated with the `Not` keyword. i.e. `Not` and `NotNull` Example: `GET /api/?nameNotIn=John,Mike&country.nameNot=Italy&ageNotBetween=20|30` ### String Filters | Parameter | Description | Example | |----------|----------|----------| |`In` | Filters the data based on whether the field's value is in a list of specified values. This filter is case sensitive. | `GET /api/?nameIn=John,Charlie` | |`StartsWith` | Filters the data based on whether the field's value begin with a specified value. This filter is case insensitive. | `GET /api/?nameStartsWith=Joh` | |`EndsWith` | Filters the data based on whether the field's value ends with a specified value. This filter is case insensitive | `GET /api/?nameEndsWith=ohn` | |`Regex` | Filters the data based on whether the field's value matches a custom PERL Regular Expression. | `GET /api/?nameRegex=/m{1,4}uel/i` | |`Contains` | Filters the data based on whether the field's value contains a specified substring. This filter is case insensitive. | `GET /api/?nameContains=harli` | ### Numeric and Date Filters | Parameter | Description | Example | |----------|----------|----------| |`MinorThan` | Filters the data based on whether the field's value is less/fewer than the specified value. (Alias of `Before`.) | `GET /api/?ageMinorThan=30` | |`MinorEqualThan` | Filters the data based on whether the field's value is less/fewer than or equal to the specified value (Alias of `BeforeIncluded`.) | `GET /api/?ageMinorEqualThan=30` | |`MajorThan` | Filters the data based on whether the field's value is greater than the specified value. (Alias of `After`.) | `GET /api/?ageMajorThan=20` | |`MajorEqualThan` | Filters the data based on whether the field's value is greater than or equal to the specified value. (Alias of `AfterIncluded`.) | `GET /api/?ageMajorEqualThan=20` | |`Between` | Filters the data based on whether the field's value is between two specified values, extremes not included. | GET /api/?ageBetween=20|30 | |`BetweenIncluded` | Filters the data based on whether the field's value is between two specified values, extremes included. | GET /api/?ageBetweenIncluded=20|30 |
